minutes.headline: Planning Board continued the Highfield Village hearing to Sept 14 with re-notice, 3-2; released two Elmwood Road lots.
minutes.summary: The board released two lots at 50 Elmwood Road, opened the 270 Electric Ave self-storage development plan review and continued it to June 8 pending peer review, and continued the long-running Highfield Village hearing to September 14 after a new engineering firm took over. It also approved minutes, heard committee reports and a town meeting recap, and voted to ask the Selectmen to name a meeting room for Marion Benson.

budget_items.what_was_said: Remaining lots are secured by a bond to be posted; the board agreed to endorse the bond form while the amount is set between the town and developer with engineer advice.
The applicant wants to avoid paying a new application fee, and the board noted it could waive fees if the application were withdrawn and refiled.

budget_items.topic: Old school building demolition and contingency
budget_items.what_was_said: A suggestion was floated to use leftover school project contingency to demolish the TC Passios building.

decisions.decision: Applicant to provide building elevations and roof lines for 270 Electric Ave before the continued hearing.
Board will endorse the bond form for 50 Elmwood Road; the amount is left to the planning director, developer and engineers.
Board asked Highfield Village applicant to submit updated traffic counts with any revised submittal.
Planning director recommended starting zoning work with a use table and districts, then parking and signs.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the long-running Highfield Village public hearing to September 14, with abutter re-notice, on a 3-2 vote.
The board continued the 270 Electric Ave self-storage hearing to June 8, and the applicant is to provide building elevations and roof lines first.
The board released two lots at 50 Elmwood Road and agreed to endorse the bond form, with the bond amount left to the planning director, developer and engineers.
The board asked the Highfield Village applicant to submit updated traffic counts with any revised submittal.
The board voted to send the Selectmen a letter asking that the conference room be named for Marion Benson.

why_it_matters: The Highfield Village development stays undecided until at least September, and abutters will be re-notified before the hearing resumes.

The 50 Elmwood Road bond is the security that covers unfinished work on the remaining lots, and its amount is still to be set outside a public vote, so the protection it gives the town is not yet known.
watch_next: June 8 at 6:35 pm: continued public hearing on the 270 Electric Ave self-storage plan, after peer review.
September 14 at 6:35 pm: continued Highfield Village hearing, with abutter re-notice and updated traffic counts.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the Elmwood Road lot release, the bond arrangement and the Marion Benson letter, though the vote count on the letter differs from what we recorded and several attendee names were misheard. Our minutes also include two continued-hearing votes, a Highfield Village traffic-count request and a zoning-work recommendation that the official minutes do not record, so check the official text for those hearings.
